summary: The note retells the opening of the Oedipus myth. Laius and Jocasta, king and queen of Thebes, consulted the Oracle of Apollo at Delphi after being childless for some time, and were told any son born to Laius would kill him. When Jocasta bore a son, Laius had the infant's ankles pierced and tethered so he could not crawl, and ordered him exposed on a nearby mountain. A servant instead passed the baby on to a Corinthian shepherd, who gave him to another shepherd.
one_line: Summarizes the birth of Oedipus, the prophecy of Apollo's Oracle at Delphi, and the infant's exposure on a mountain near Thebes.
key_facts: Oedipus was the son of Laius and Jocasta, king and queen of Thebes.
Laius and Jocasta had been childless for some time before Laius consulted the Oracle of Apollo at Delphi.
The Oracle prophesied that any son born to Laius would kill him.
When Jocasta bore a son, Laius had the baby's ankles pierced and tethered together so that he could not crawl.
Jocasta gave the boy to a servant to be exposed on the nearby mountain.
Laius intended for the child to die of exposure.
The servant did not leave the child to die of exposure as Laius intended.
The servant passed the baby on to a shepherd from Corinth.
That Corinthian shepherd gave the child to another shepherd.
